assumptions: Starting point: the longest task the newest model can do at 80% reliability (claude_opus_4_6_inspect, released 2026-02-05: 69.87 minutes, METR).
Office work counts as 50 times harder for AI than METR's software tasks (METR's study of other domains).
No delay is added for companies to start using AI: every date means AI could do the task, not that it will.
Slowdown scenario: the published delays at 80% reliability (Whitfill, Snodin & Becker). The authors call it illustrative.
A task counts as "AI could do this" once the year passes the middle of its date range.
Tasks with no published time in Anthropic's data are never counted as something AI could do.
Match score (our weighting): skills 40%, fit with what's left of your week 30%, job outlook 30%. A missing skill in the same ESCO group as one you have counts 0.5.

Market + planet ranking (our weighting): each SDG goal a job helps adds 5 points (or takes them away if it harms it), 10 if Malaysia is off track on that goal (SDSN, off track on goals 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16, 17). Each goal counts once per job, and the total is at most 15 points either way.

Skill labels for a year: robust = some task in our data using the skill is still human after that year in every scenario; bet = only in some (in practice, only if AI slows down); trap = in none. Tasks with no published time are left out, so a skill never looks safe only because data is missing.
Skill weather: whether the skill is a bigger (rising), smaller (declining) or the same (steady) part of the still-human hours of your week than today, under the chosen scenario.
Route weeks assume 3.5 hours of study a week. Course cost and length are as written on the course page on the date checked. HRD Corp status is not checked.
Name and age are never used in any calculation.
